subject: Anthropic Haiku 5.5 💸, OpenAI GPT-6 Intelligent UI 🖥️, Google Playgrou
intro: The AI pricing floor just got lower. Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/M tokens matches GPT-6 Luna exactly, and that's not a coincidence. Both labs are racing to make inference so cheap it becomes a non-decision for developers. Meanwhile, OpenAI is quietly redefining what an "answer" even means. Interactive UIs, live calculators, clickable diagrams inside chat. The text box era is ending faster than we expected. Cheap tokens plus richer interfaces. We're watching the commoditization of intelligence happen in real time.

news.headline: Anthropic drops Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest small model at 75% lower cost
news.body: Anthropic just dropped Claude Haiku 5.5 , and the headline is the price. It costs 90% less per token than Haiku 4.5 for most requests, landing at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. There is one catch worth knowing before you migrate: that cheap rate only applies to prompts under 100,000 tokens. Go over that, and the price jumps 5x. The good news? About 90% of real requests stay under that limit anyway. Here is what you can actually do with it now: It also ships with a 1 million token context window and 128K max output. Available now on AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure via model ID claude-haiku-5-5 .
bullets: Run high-volume tasks like summaries and classification at near-zero cost
Use it as a cheap subagent alongside Sonnet or Opus for coding pipelines
Power live customer support and browser automation, it is fast enough
Tune the effort setting (low to max) to trade speed for smarts per task

news.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-6 with interactive visuals, buttons, and tools inside ChatGPT
news.body: ChatGPT just stopped being a text box. GPT-6 with Intelligent UI is rolling out now, and it changes what an "answer" actually looks like. Instead of walls of text, ChatGPT now picks the best format for your question automatically. Ask something complex, and it might hand you a clickable diagram. Ask for help budgeting, and it builds you a working calculator right inside the chat. Here's what you can actually do with it: Two model versions power this: GPT-6 Sol for paid tiers, GPT-6 Luna for Free and Go. Both handle everyday conversation. This only affects the Chat tab, not Work or Codex. The big unlock here is that ChatGPT now builds mini-apps around your question on demand. No coding needed.
bullets: Get interactive charts and diagrams that respond as you explore them
Use tappable buttons and forms built on the spot for your specific task
Play games or run calculators generated live in your conversation
Get partial answers faster while the model is still thinking

news.headline: Google Labs launches Playground, a no-code AI game creation tool
news.body: Someone just dropped a platform that lets you build and play your own games with zero coding required. It's called Playground , and the pitch is simple: if you can imagine a game, you can make it. No engines. No syntax errors. No tutorials to grind through. Here's what makes it interesting for you: For CS students, this is worth watching. It shows where AI-assisted creation is heading: you bring the idea, the machine handles execution. Currently available in the US for users 18+.
bullets: You describe what you want, and the platform builds it, meaning AI is doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes
It opens up game creation to anyone who has ideas but not the time to learn Unity or Unreal
It's a live experiment in how far natural language interfaces (just typing what you want in plain English) can replace traditional tools
